stem: A 40-year-old man recently started a medication to help him stay abstinent from alcohol. Twenty minutes after a single beer he has facial flushing, palpitations, headache and vomiting, with a blood pressure of 88/54 mm Hg.
oneliner: 40M + new alcohol-abstinence drug + flushing, palpitations, headache, vomiting 20 min after a beer + BP 88/54 → which drug?
ask: Which drug was he most likely started on?

whyNot.B: An **opioid antagonist** that cuts craving; it does **not cause a reaction to alcohol**
whyNot.C: Modulates **NMDA/GABA** to reduce craving; drinking on it does **not cause flushing**
whyNot.D: Blocks **alcohol dehydrogenase** for methanol or ethylene glycol; it would **slow** ethanol breakdown, not raise acetaldehyde
whyNot.E: A **benzodiazepine** for withdrawal; it does not cause a **reaction to a drink**

why: **Disulfiram** inhibits **aldehyde dehydrogenase**, so alcohol causes **acetaldehyde build-up** with flushing, tachycardia, nausea and hypotension. It mimics the reaction seen in **ALDH2-deficient** East Asian drinkers.

drug.name: Disulfiram
drug.how: Irreversibly blocks aldehyde dehydrogenase so acetaldehyde accumulates after alcohol
drug.use: Deterrent in alcohol use disorder for motivated patients
drug.watch: Flushing, tachycardia, nausea, hypotension with any alcohol; hepatotoxicity; metallic taste

idea.rule: Acetaldehyde build-up causes the flushing reaction, whether the enzyme is blocked by a drug or missing by genetics.
also: ALDH2*2 variant in East Asians: flushing after alcohol
Cephalosporins with an MTT side chain (cefotetan): disulfiram-like reaction

stem: A 28-year-old man with familial hypertriglyceridemia and recurrent pancreatitis is started on gemfibrozil. Three months later he has episodes of colicky right upper quadrant pain after fatty meals. Creatine kinase and liver enzymes are normal.
oneliner: 28M + familial hypertriglyceridemia + recurrent pancreatitis + gemfibrozil started + colicky RUQ pain after fatty meals + normal CK and liver enzymes → adverse effect?
ask: Which adverse effect of this drug is most likely?

options.A: Flushing and itching of the skin
options.D: High uric acid with gout attacks

whyNot.A: Typical of **niacin** (prostaglandin-mediated); it does not explain **biliary pain**
whyNot.B: Typical of **bile acid resins**; this drug **lowers** triglycerides and the pain is **biliary**
whyNot.C: Typical of **ACE inhibitors**; this man has **right upper quadrant pain after fatty meals**
whyNot.D: Typical of **niacin** and thiazides; gout does not cause **colicky right upper quadrant pain after fatty meals**

why: **Gemfibrozil** is a **fibrate** that activates **PPAR-alpha**, raising lipoprotein lipase and lowering VLDL. It also inhibits **cholesterol 7-alpha-hydroxylase**, so less cholesterol becomes bile acid and bile is supersaturated, causing **cholesterol gallstones**; **myopathy** is also a risk, especially with a **statin**.

drug.name: Gemfibrozil
drug.how: Activates PPAR-alpha, increasing lipoprotein lipase and lowering VLDL and triglycerides
drug.watch: Cholesterol gallstones, myopathy (especially with statins), raised liver enzymes

idea.rule: Each lipid drug has a signature adverse effect.
also: Bile acid resins: GI upset, raised triglycerides
Ezetimibe: diarrhea, rarely liver enzyme rise
